canonical.title: Maximum Width of Binary Tree
canonical.sourceFilePath: 11. Binary Trees/3. Hard/03. Max width of binary tree.cpp

narrative.title: The Loading Dock Span Audit
narrative.scenario: A fulfilment hub draws its storage map as a binary tree, and safety inspectors measure each floor's span by counting the gaps between its outermost occupied bays — phantom bays in between still count toward the span. The audit report must publish the widest floor ever measured across the whole warehouse.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child).
narrative.outputFormat: Return the maximum width — the largest count of node slots, including null gaps, between the leftmost and rightmost node of any level.

testCases.explanation: The last level stretches from slot 0 (5) to slot 3 (9): 5, phantom, phantom, 9 — a span of 4.
The deepest level holds only 5 and 3 side by side, so the widest span is 2.

hintLevels: Level 1: Walk the tree floor by floor and track how far apart the end bays of each floor sit.
Level 2: Hand every node a positional index — child slots are 2*i and 2*i+1 of the parent's — and store indices alongside nodes in the queue.
Level 3: Re-base each level's indices so the front of the queue is zero; overflow-safe width is last index minus first plus one.
